title: Swift Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Print a greeting
examples.description: print shows a value and ends the line. Text inside quotes is a String.

examples.title: Keep a fixed value
examples.description: let makes a constant. Its value cannot be changed after it is set.

examples.title: Change a value
examples.description: var makes a variable that can change. += adds to its current value.

examples.title: Put a value in text
examples.description: A backslash followed by parentheses places a value inside a Swift string.

examples.title: Choose a message
examples.description: if checks a Boolean rule, which is either true or false.
examples.code:
let score = 8
if score >= 5 { print("Pass") } else { print("Try again") }

examples.title: Read an array item
examples.description: An array keeps values of one type in order. Position zero is first.

examples.title: Name reusable steps
examples.description: A function takes an input and returns a typed result. _ lets callers omit the input label.
examples.code:
func twice(_ n: Int) -> Int { n * 2 }
print(twice(4))

examples.title: Choose a fallback
examples.description: An optional can hold a value or nil. ?? gives a fallback when it is nil.

examples.title: Read only when present
examples.description: if let unwraps an optional only when it contains a value.
examples.code:
let score: Int? = 8
if let value = score { print(value) }

examples.title: Group fields with a struct
examples.description: A struct groups related values. A Book has a title and a page count.

examples.title: Name a few choices
examples.description: An enum lists a fixed set of choices. switch handles each possible choice.
